title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Sofia Martin
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical sales enablement materials for field reps and solution engineers: positioning and messaging, competitive brief, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this deck for discovery, qualification, and POC handoffs; link to product and security pages for technical deep dives.

Audience: Sales, pre-sales (SEs), partner reps, and marketing content owners.

Key outcomes:
- Consistent, engineering-first positioning and one-line elevator pitch.
- Short competitive one-pagers for common objection handling.
- Recommended pitch-deck flow and slide-level talking points.
- Pricing guidance and packaging guardrails for hosted, Dedicated, and Private motions.
- Three repeatable case study summaries and impact metrics.
- Security FAQ for prospects to accelerate procurement and legal review.

---

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Elevator (1-line): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable, cost-efficient, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Top three value props (use in this order):
1. Production-first performance and reliability: predictable tail latency, autoscaling, and multi-layer fallbacks keep user-facing experiences available under load.
2. Cost and operational control: intelligent batching, caching, and quantization recommendations that reduce token unit economics without sacrificing quality.
3. Unified deployment model: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) for simplified rollouts and compliance.

Elevator (30s pitch):
- Problem: Customers struggle to move from experiments to production because serving LLMs at scale requires specialized runtime, heavy ops, and unpredictable cost.
- Solution: Redwood abstracts the serving runtime and ops while exposing cost- and performance-levers to engineering teams.
- Why now: Growth of open models and heterogeneous hardware means serving, not model ownership, becomes the differentiator.

Evidence bullets (one-liners to use in pitch):
- Verified latency profiles across curated open models (link in related pages).
- Customer X reduced per-token inference cost by 3.2x after adopting batching and KV caching.
- SLAs and Dedicated capacity options for enterprise customers with strict uptime requirements.

Message hierarchy (for playbook):
- Use the 1-line elevator for top-of-funnel.
- Use the 30s pitch in discovery and SDR handoffs.
- Use evidence bullets and case study metrics in product demos and economic justification.

---

2) Competitive Brief (short form)

Summary: Focus on three competitor archetypes and top rebuttals.

Competitor matrix (high-level):
||Competitor||What they offer||Redwood advantage||Primary objection and rebuttal||
|OpenAI (hosted)||Broad developer APIs, managed infrastructure||Lower cost controls, Dedicated & Private deployments, and deterministic latency SLOs||"OpenAI is easiest" -> Redwood offers same simplicity plus predictable economics and on-prem options|
|Cloud-managed (AWS SageMaker/Azure OpenAI)||Enterprise integrations and cloud portfolio||Redwood provides inference-optimized runtime with better unit economics and unified cross-cloud routing||"One vendor for cloud is simpler" -> Redwood reduces vendor lock-in with multi-region routing and fallbacks|
|Self-hosted runtimes (internal infra or open-source stack)||Full control, but high ops burden||Faster time-to-value, production-grade fallbacks, and ops tooling to reduce maintenance overhead||"We want full control" -> Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) retains control while handling orchestration and updates|

Top competitive plays and rebuttals (quick bullets):
- If they say "we can self-host": emphasize TCO (ops headcount, uplift time, reliability incidents) and offer a pilot with Dedicated capacity.
- If they point to a competitor's model catalog: highlight Redwood-verified performance profiles and model-level rollouts + fallbacks.
- If they raise security/compliance: point to Private deployment options, audit logging, KMS/HSM integrations, and our compliance evidence pack.

---

3) Pitch Deck Outline (recommended 10-12 slides)

Slide flow and talking points:
1. Title & one-liner (use elevator).
2. Agenda and what we will cover.
3. Market context and why serving matters (latency/cost/ops).
4. Customer challenges: variability, cost, ops overhead.
5. Redwood solution overview: runtime + orchestration + tooling.
6. Demo / architecture diagram (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
7. Performance & cost evidence (benchmarks and customer metrics).
8. Security & compliance summary (links to deeper docs).
9. Pricing overview and packaging options.
10. Case study #1 (SaaS search), #2 (enterprise assistant), #3 (regulated industry).
11. Pilot proposal & next steps (POC success criteria, timeline, ownership).
12. Appendix: detailed benchmarks, integration checklist, SLOs.

Slide-level tips:
- Use charts for latency distribution and per-token cost change after optimization.
- SEs: prepare a simple architecture diagram mapping prospect infra to Redwood connectors (VPC peering, Private control plane, KMS).
- For enterprise buyers include an appendix slide with SLA details: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated, target p50/p95 latency numbers by model class.

---

4) Pricing Guidance & Packaging (field-facing guardrails)

Pricing principles (how to speak about price):
- Be transparent: break out per-token hosted pricing vs Dedicated commit vs Private fixed fee + usage.
- Tie pricing to value: show ROI via cost reduction (batching, cache) and improved conversion from low-latency UX.
- Use tiers: Self-serve (hosted) -> Reserved (Dedicated) -> Enterprise (Private + support).

Representative packages (talking points not contractual):
- Hosted API: pay-as-you-go per-token for generation/embeddings, free tier for quick POC, volume discounts at milestones.
- Dedicated: monthly committed GPU capacity with burst pricing and autoscaling; recommended for customers with predictable throughput (>X QPS).
- Private: license + deployment fee for VPC or on-prem, optional managed service add-on for 24/7 support and quarterly updates.

Commercial play examples:
- Early startup POC: free credits, <30 day pilot, hosted pricing, conversion play to Dedicated once sustained usage observed.
- Mid-market product team: recommend 3-month Dedicated trial with predefined SLOs and capacity sizing workshop.
- Regulated enterprise: Private deployment + professional services, attach SOC/ISO evidence and encryption options.

Contracting notes for sales/legal handoffs:
- Include clear SLAs for Dedicated with uptime credits.
- Define data handling and retention in SOW for Private deployments.
- Offer a 90-day rollback/upgrade window during initial rollout for major model changes.

---

5) Case Studies (triage-ready summaries for decks / emails)

1) SaaS Search Company (Customer A) - Outcome: 42% reduction in median latency and 3.2x reduction in per-query inference cost.
- Challenge: Search relevance and latency spikes during peak hours.
- Redwood solution: Dedicated GPU pool, KV cache for common prefixes, and model quantization recommendations.
- Impact: Improved conversion, reduced infra spend; contract expanded to Dedicated.

2) Enterprise Virtual Assistant (Customer B) - Outcome: 99.95% availability with multi-region fallbacks and audit logging.
- Challenge: Strict uptime and audit requirements across global offices.
- Redwood solution: Dedicated pools with cross-region routing and Private deployment for PII-sensitive flows.
- Impact: Passed security review, fast product launch in three regions.

3) Regulated Financial Services (Customer C) - Outcome: Achieved data residency requirements and streamlined procurement.
- Challenge: On-prem / air-gapped requirements and KMS/HSM-integrated key management.
- Redwood solution: Private on-prem package with HSM integration and compliance evidence pack.
- Impact: Closed a multi-year enterprise deal; lower legal friction.

One-page case study template (use for rapid content creation):
- Headline metric
- Customer profile and industry
- Challenge (1-2 sentences)
- Redwood approach (1-3 bullets)
- Measurable outcomes (metrics)
- Quote + next steps (if available)

---

6) Security FAQ (prospect-facing, short answers)

Q: Where will customer data be stored and processed?
A: Hosted API processes data in our managed cloud regions; Dedicated keeps inference on isolated GPU pools; Private lets customers keep control (VPC/on-prem). We document region and residency options per contract.

Q: Do you support customer-managed encryption keys?
A: Yes. We support KMS integrations and HSM-backed key management for Private deployments and Dedicated configurations where required.

Q: Can we run Redwood in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. We offer an on-prem Private package specifically for air-gapped deployments; it includes installation artifacts, offline update guidance, and professional services.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are provided?
A: Audit logging is available across Hosted (limited retention), Dedicated, and Private (customer-controlled). Logs can be exported to customer SIEM via secure connectors.

Q: How do you prevent model data leakage or prompt logging exposure?
A: We provide opt-in prompt redaction, configurable retention policies, and ability to disable logging for sensitive routes in Private deployments.

Q: What compliance evidence is available?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II evidence, ISO readiness notes, and a compliance evidence pack for enterprise procurement. For regulated customers we provide architecture diagrams and runbook extracts.

Q: How do you handle vulnerability disclosure and security incidents?
A: We follow our incident response policy; customers are notified per contract SLA and we provide post-incident reports and remediation plans.

Q: Who has access to customer data within Redwood?
A: Access is RBAC controlled, with SSO integrations and least-privilege defaults. Elevated access requires documented approvals and audit trails.

---

7) Objections, Rebuttals & Battle Cards

Common objections and short scripts:
- "We already use OpenAI / cloud vendor": "Great - many customers use multiple providers. Redwood reduces variance in latency and cost and can act as a consistent layer across providers or be used privately for regulated workloads."
- "We want full on-prem control": "We offer Private on-prem with professional services and a handoff plan. Many customers choose Private to accelerate compliance while retaining control."
- "Your pricing is higher than open-source self-hosted": "Self-hosting has hidden costs - ops, downtime, and maintenance. We'll model TCO and run a 90-day pilot to demonstrate run-rate savings through batching/caching."

Battle-card quick references (to hand to SDRs/SEs):
- 1-pager competitive bullets (use Competitive matrix above).
- Pilot checklist (POC success criteria, data samples, endpoint integration, latency/cost targets).
- Security checklist (required evidence, deployment types, lead time estimates).

---

8) Pilot / POC Playbook (high level steps)

1. Discovery (1-2 meetings): define traffic profile, SLOs, data residency requirements, and success metrics.
2. Pilot design (SE + customer): choose Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; define sample dataset and integration method.
3. Setup (1-2 weeks typical): create API keys or provision Dedicated pool / Private node; configure logging and SLO tracking.
4. Run & measure (2-6 weeks): capture latency distribution, token cost, and quality metrics vs baseline.
5. Review & recommend: present findings, recommended optimizations (batching/quantization), and commercial conversion options.

Success criteria examples:
- p95 latency target met for interactive use cases.
- >= 2x improvement in cost-per-inference or acceptable tradeoff between cost and quality.
- Security checklist items validated for enterprise.
